decisions.question: METR 80% time horizon exceeds 10h before September
decisions.thinking: METR's August 19 evaluation of GPT-5.6 Sol constitutes an August announcement, pushing the resolution window to Dec 1 under the market rules. Although METR avoided picking a single point estimate due to treatment variance (ranging from 11h to 270h+), the lower bound of treatments exceeds 10 hours. Accounting for the strictness of the 80% reliability threshold, I estimate an 18% chance this resolves YES.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether METR will issue a single point estimate or declare the 80% time horizon 'likely greater than 10h' for GPT-5.6 Sol before December 1.
decisions.resolution_risk: The market will not resolve NO immediately on August 31 if the creator treats the August 19 release as an unmeasured August announcement, extending resolution to December 1.
evidence_for: METR published a pre-deployment evaluation for GPT-5.6 Sol on August 19, 2026, fulfilling the August announcement condition.
Treatment point estimates reported in commentary for GPT-5.6 Sol ranged from 11 hours to over 270 hours, all of which exceed 10 hours.
evidence_against: METR explicitly stated that no single point estimate should be selected as a general-purpose time horizon due to cheating rates and treatment variability.
An 80% task completion time horizon requires 80% success rate on long tasks, which is significantly stricter than a 50% time horizon and may be well under 10 hours.

decisions.question: Will the AfD win an absolute majority in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt in 2026
decisions.thinking: While AfD is polling strongly at 41-42%, converting this into an outright Landtag seat majority (>50%) requires a high wasted vote share (parties <5%) and no late-stage polling erosion or anti-AfD tactical mobilization. An absolute majority remains possible but is less likely than current market pricing implies.
decisions.uncertainty: The exact total vote share of parties failing to clear the 5% threshold and whether tactical voting boosts the SPD, Greens, or Die Linke into parliament.
decisions.resolution_risk: Overhang and compensatory mandates (Überhang- und Ausgleichsmandate) altering the total parliament size, though proportional seat distribution generally aligns closely with valid vote proportions above 5%.
evidence_for: AfD leads polling substantially at 41% to 42%, well ahead of the CDU at ~24%.

Several smaller parties (e.g., Greens, FDP, Die Linke) are at risk of missing the 5% electoral threshold, which would elevate the seat share of parties clearing the hurdle and lower the effective vote threshold needed for an absolute majority.
evidence_against: Securing more than 50% of parliamentary seats from a ~41% vote share requires a substantial fraction of wasted votes (parties below 5%) and zero underperformance on election day.
Tactical voting campaigns are mobilizing support for mainstream smaller parties (such as SPD) to ensure they clear 5% and deny an outright AfD majority.
Historical precedent across modern German state elections makes single-party absolute majorities exceedingly rare under proportional representation with compensatory mandates.
